items.title: What I Checked
items.why:
I audited the art sheet and the ChatGPT prompt. Nothing has been changed.

Every finding was checked against the app's code, the Dragon Ball art files, or OpenAI's own docs and forum. The last item is the audit of this audit: what I got wrong or dropped.

Found: 3 errors, 7 blind spots, 1 speed issue, 1 heads-up about the code, and 6 ideas.

items.title: ChatGPT May Not Be Able to Read the Sheet
items.why:
The descriptions of all 68 pictures are only on the sheet; the prompt says "see the sheet". The sheet is 2400 x 3760 px. OpenAI's docs and forum say large uploads are shrunk before the model reads them, often to about 768 px wide. At that size the descriptions are about 6 px tall and the Dragon Ball references are thumbnails.

Left: part of the sheet at full size. Right: the same part shrunk to 768 px wide.

options.label: Words in the prompt, one sheet per group
options.desc: All 68 descriptions go in the prompt as plain text (always readable). The sheet becomes 5 smaller sheets, one per group, sent with that group's request.

options.label: Words in the prompt only
options.desc: Keep one sheet as a visual map; the descriptions move into the prompt.

options.label: Keep as is
options.desc: One sheet, descriptions only on it.

items.title: The Scouter Picture Is Square, Not Wide
items.why: The sheet says scouter.png should be "Wide". The Dragon Ball file is 420 x 420, and the app shows it at 300 x 300. A wide picture would be squashed or cut off.

items.title: "Replaces" Sounds Like Overwriting Dragon Ball
items.why: Every tile says "replaces pose/wave.png" and so on. Rob and Lennon keep the Dragon Ball look, so nothing is replaced. The new files need their own folder, and the same names in two places is how files get mixed up.

options.label: "Dragon Ball version" + own folder
options.desc: Tiles say "Dragon Ball version: pose/wave.png" and every new file is saved as img/eras/... (for example img/eras/pose/wave.png).

items.title: The Sheet and the Prompt Disagree on Sizes
items.why: The sheet says bracelets are 512 px, profile pictures 512 px and icons 256 px. The prompt asks for 7, 19 and 17 of them on one ChatGPT image, whose largest size is 1536 x 1024. That makes each one about 200 to 300 px. ChatGPT gets two different instructions.

options.label: One rule: "as large as fits"
options.desc: Both say: make each item as large as the grid allows; I resize to the app's sizes (2x for sharp phone screens) and compress.

items.title: Transparent Backgrounds Often Fail
items.why: OpenAI's own guide says asking for a transparent background doesn't guarantee one, and their forum has a long thread of ChatGPT users getting a painted checkerboard or white instead. The prompt relies on it for all 68 pictures.

options.label: Flat magenta background; I remove it
options.desc: Ask for a solid #FF00FF background with nothing magenta in the art. I cut it out here and check every edge on light and dark screens.

options.label: Ask for transparent; I check each file
options.desc: Keep the request; I test each file's transparency and send back any that fail.

options.label: Use Adobe's background remover
options.desc: Your Adobe account's Remove Background on each picture.

items.title: Big Grids Drift
items.why: Image models are unreliable at exact counts and even spacing. 19 avatars in a 5 x 4 grid can come back as 18 or 20, touching, or out of order, and each item gets less detail.

options.label: Groups of 4 (2 x 2)
options.desc: About 15 requests instead of 4. Each item is bigger and more detailed, and a bad one is cheap to redo.

options.label: One picture per request
options.desc: Best quality, 68 requests.

options.label: Keep the big grids
options.desc: 4 requests; I send back any that come out wrong.

items.title: Draw Tour Cat's Model Sheet First
items.why: Animation studios lock a character with a model sheet before drawing any scenes. Today the prompt starts straight with wave.png, so the cat can change from pose to pose.

options.label: Model sheet first
options.desc: One image: Tour Cat front, side and back, plus 6 faces (happy, wink, thinking, sleepy, fierce, proud). Every pose request attaches it.

options.label: Start with wave.png
options.desc: As written.

items.title: The Style References Are Thumbnails
items.why: Each Dragon Ball reference on the sheet is 110 px, and smaller after shrinking. "Same style" is the most important instruction, and its evidence is the smallest thing on the page.

options.label: Attach 5 full-size style examples
options.desc: yougotthis, restday, a profile picture (Vegeta), a Dragon Ball and an icon, at full size, as the style guide.

items.title: Dark Screens
items.why: The Eras look has a dark mode (deep purple, #1c1530). The Dragon Ball art has no light edge, so dark outlines and black areas blend in a little on dark screens (see the hair and banner). The Eras set has more dark subjects: the Reputation snake, the black-and-white typewriter and the midnight ring.

now.caption: Dragon Ball art on the Eras dark background

options.label: A thin light rim on dark subjects
options.desc: Ask for a soft pink-white rim light on dark shapes (snake, typewriter, black hair), and I check every picture on light and dark before it goes in.

options.label: White sticker edge on everything
options.desc: Every picture gets a thin white outline. Clearest, but a small style difference from Dragon Ball.

options.label: Match Dragon Ball exactly
options.desc: No edge, as today.

items.title: Pictures Shown Tiny
items.why: Some pictures are shown much smaller than drawn: the bead charm at 24 px, the thinking cat at 56 px, the menu icons at 26 to 28 px, and the Pro Tips cat at 120 px. The prompt only warns about one of them.

options.label: List every display size
options.desc: Each description says its real size on screen, and the small ones are asked for as simpler, bolder shapes. I check each at real size before it goes in.

items.title: Two Scottish Fold Cats
items.why: Tour Cat and the grey cat avatar are both Scottish Folds, so in the avatar picker they could look like the same cat.

options.label: Give Tour Cat her own colours
options.desc: For example a cream-and-lavender coat with pink ear tips, so no other cat looks like her.

options.label: Change the grey cat instead
options.desc: For example a tabby, keeping the ragdoll.

items.title: Era Details I Assumed
items.why: A few era colours and objects came from memory, notably the Showgirl colours (orange and mint) and the exact Debut shade. A wrong detail is the kind of thing a fan spots right away.

options.label: Check each era first
options.desc: I check every era's colours and symbols against reliable sources before the prompt goes out.

options.label: Ask Alice
options.desc: She checks the 12 era descriptions; I build in her edits.

items.title: Every Phone Would Download Every Look
items.why: The app saves all its art for offline use on every phone (sw.js keeps one list of all art). 68 new pictures, about 1 MB at Dragon Ball's sizes, would land on Rob's and Lennon's phones too, though they never see them.

options.label: Each phone saves only the looks it uses
options.desc: Dragon Ball phones skip the Eras art and the other way round. A look's art downloads when a profile on that phone switches to it.

options.label: Save everything, but smaller
options.desc: WebP files, about 30 to 50% smaller.

items.title: Several Pictures Need Code to Show
items.why: Some Dragon Ball pictures only appear for the Dragon Ball look today: the scouter popup (scouter.js line 71), the rest-day card (homecards.js line 35), the workout cheers (engine.js line 398) and the finale (milestones.js line 121). The avatar picker shows bracelets for other looks (avatar.js line 90). The art alone won't make them appear in the Eras look; that's part of building the skin. I'll also write words for screen readers for each new picture.

items.title: The 7 Bracelets Tell a Story
items.why: Today each bracelet only differs by its number of star beads.

options.label: Each bracelet is one era
options.desc: 1 Debut teal, 2 Fearless gold, 3 Speak Now purple, 4 Red, 5 1989 sky blue, 6 Reputation black and silver, 7 Lover pink. Collecting all 7 is touring the eras.

options.label: Same bracelet, more stars
options.desc: As written.

items.title: What a Bracelet Looks Like Before You Earn It
items.why: Today the unearned bracelet is the same bracelet faded to grey.

options.label: Loose beads on a string
options.desc: Unearned = plain undyed beads half-strung on a loose cord, waiting to be made. Earning it "makes" the bracelet.

options.label: Faded grey copy
options.desc: As written.

items.title: Tour Cat Changes Outfits
items.why: One combined Eras Tour look could show through Tour Cat herself, the way the real show changes costumes between eras.

options.label: A different era outfit per pose
options.desc: For example a sparkly Lover bodysuit to wave, the folklore cardigan for rest day, a Reputation snake-print jacket for "Let's Train!", a Midnights star dress for the finale. Same cat, same face.

options.label: One outfit everywhere
options.desc: The rhinestone bodysuit in every pose.

items.title: The Finale Picture
items.why: It shows when all 7 are collected, like Shenron.

options.label: Reputation snake from the bracelets
options.desc: As written: a glittering black-and-silver snake coiling up out of the 7 bracelets.

options.label: Surprise-song stage
options.desc: A glowing piano and acoustic guitar on a lit stage, fireworks bursting from the 7 bracelets.

options.label: Tour Cat takes a bow
options.desc: Tour Cat on a stage platform rising through fireworks, the 7 bracelets on her arm.

items.title: Banner Words
items.why: The banners copy Dragon Ball's words: "Let's Train!", "You Got This!", "Rest Day".

options.label: Tour words
options.desc: "It's Showtime!", "You Got This!", "Rest Day" with a small "Encore tomorrow". The app's words for each look come with the skin build.

items.title: What I Corrected or Dropped
items.why:
Corrected: I first assumed the Dragon Ball art has a white sticker edge. It doesn't (see Dark Screens), so that item now offers a light rim as a choice instead of saying the prompt left one out.

Less certain than it sounds: the 768 px shrink comes from OpenAI's older docs and forum posts. Newer models can read larger images. Putting the words in the prompt costs nothing either way, so the recommendation stands.

Not certain: OpenAI's docs disagree on which image models do transparency. The magenta-background route works whichever model ChatGPT uses.

Dropped: a finding that banner text might be misspelled (I check every file anyway), and that ChatGPT's output files are large (I resize and compress them as part of putting them in).

Own error, already fixed earlier: I first said 58 pictures; it's 68.

Not checked: the sheet in a real ChatGPT chat. A 1-picture trial (wave.png) would show how ChatGPT handles it before you spend time on all 68.

options.label: Do the 1-picture trial first
options.desc: You send ChatGPT just the wave.png request; we fix the brief from what comes back.

items.title: After You Pick
items.why: I'll rewrite the prompt and sheet exactly as you picked, check them again, and send both back. Nothing in the app changes.

options.label: Show me first
options.desc: Pictures of the new sheet before the final files.
